evidence: Route 1, per-item published statistics (verify_li_2021_knowledge_sharing.R). A one-factor CFA on the live 336x4 data reproduces the paper's Table 2 standardized loadings and SEs per code: KS1 0.7938/0.0244 vs published 0.794/0.024, KS2 0.8199/0.0221 vs 0.820/0.022, KS3 0.8804/0.0180 vs 0.880/0.018, KS4 0.8266/0.0215 vs 0.827/0.022 -- largest |loading diff| 0.0004, largest |SE diff| 0.0005. Table 2 is a PNG; none of these numbers appear in the article text. Rival sweep over 10 permutations of the published loadings: every rival touching KS1 or KS3 scores >= 0.026 (worst 0.086 for the KS1<->KS3 swap), so those two are separated outright, but the KS2<->KS4 swap scores 0.0074 (published 0.820 vs 0.827, identical SE 0.022) and is NOT excluded. The text-to-code tie itself is an explicit code-label match, not a data test: S1 Appendix heads the block 'Knowledge Sharing（KS）' and numbers 4 items 1-4 against the S2 header's KS1..KS4, corroborated across the whole file (appendix blocks of 12/4/9/6 numbered items vs header blocks CQ1-12, KS1-4, OCD1-9, SIB1-6; 41 columns = ID + 9 covariates + 31 items), and data/li_2021_cultural_intelligence.py melts the KS-prefixed columns by name so the code IS the source header. What this does NOT establish: that appendix item n is column KSn (live item means span only 0.31 -- 4.83/5.07/5.14/4.93 -- so a permuted appendix numbering would be invisible), and the KS2/KS4 assignment. Hence PARTIAL.
